newsitem.title: UK: New UK upstream oil co launced with 3I stake.
newsitem.headline: New UK upstream oil co launced with 3I stake.

text.p: A new British oil production company was launched on Monday to tap economically marginal North Sea oilfields using state-of-the-art technology.

Aberdeen-based Venture Production said by combining new production systems, such as "smart" wells controlled by computers, with innovative financing, conventional oil field economics could be challenged.

"Venture is a new generation oil company targeted at underdeveloped oilfields which can be 'demarginalised' by the application of advanced production technology," said Larry Kinch, a director of Venture.
Venture said it has won the financial backing of Britain's leading venture capital group, 3I, which has taken a "significant" stake in the company, but declined to specify the size of the holding.

By using specialist floating production systems, Venture hopes it can commercially exploit the three billion barrels of oil equivalent which British government figures show remain in the North Sea reserve base.
Exploiting those marginal fields previously passed over by larger companies, and extracting from existing fields to their full potential, could increase oilfield value by 30 percent, Venture said.
The company is also reported to be looking at ways in which funds can be raised on derivatives markets.

The new company will work closely with an established Aberdeen oil service company, Petroleum Engineering Services (PES), of which Kinch is chairman. Leading U.S. energy services group Halliburton recently took a 26 percent stake in PES.
